questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a country that had beautiful nature. Vancouver had this, plus a university that I had heard much about. And I always wanted to visit Canada. Going on exchange, there were also a bit of comfort in going to a country that spoke English.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Stuff like that is always a bit confusing, but I found it overall easy enough to find the information that I needed upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went to the information meetings and imagine day, but other than that nothing, as I did not need it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I did not get on campus housing, so I found an airbnb with two other people from my home university. It was easy enough but it was really expensive, so in that aspect I would not recommend airbnb. Besides the price, I think it is the easiest way to do it, when you're only there for about four months. We didn't have to pay a deposit and we didn't need to buy anything for the apartment as many other people have to do when they rent a place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you want to be a part of the campus-life it will take a bit more effort, as you live further away. For me, I ended up really enjoying living off campus, as I heard that the housing on campus (Fairview) were missing a lot of things that the people had to buy, plus it was pretty run down.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not satisfied as I did not get housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registred before arriving and ended up switching out two of my classes after arrival. It was easy enough.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was help available on campus for exchange students, but I didn't need it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Before arriving, I got all the classes that I wanted, but when switching to different classes a lot of them were filled up.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the weeks at the beginning of the term where you could try all the classes you wanted before deciding. I ended up switching two of my courses for something else after coming to 1-3 classes in the first weeks and finding out that it wasn't for me. I really recommend doing this, as you get a sense of the profs teaching style and hear more about exams and expectations + attendance.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Coming from Denmark, I found the academic level a bit too low. Some of the classes were really interesting, but some were a bit "ruined" by the papers we had to do. Instead of making critical papers and using the theory we had read, it became very "summary-based" papers, where the prof just wanted to make sure that we had read the texts for that week, instead of actually wanting us to learn. In this way, it didn't feel like a university-level course. Of course, this was very nice for an exchange student, as I didn't need to stress about keeping up.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The profs had a more pedagogical approach. This was in some instances nice, as they really led us through the semester, but it didn't feel very academic. At UCPH your relationship with your profs tend to feel a bit more like academic peers, which I really like.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Feminist theory
Special Topics in Gender, Race, and Sexuality
Topics in 19th-Century Philosophy
Gender and Nation: Women's State in Modern Central, Eastern and Northern European literatures and Cultures

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: "Special Topics in Gender, Race, and Sexuality" with Dr. Alifa Bandali was a really great course! Dr. Bandali is a really great teacher and the theory we used was really interesting.

questions.answer: The compass card, but it turned out to be really nice to have. Other than that, I used most of my money on travel.

questions.answer: Groceries were pretty cheep. Housing was the most expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything was available at UBC.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I heard the the surf-club or the outdoor-club were really good.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit Whistler and Vancouver Island. There are a lot to do very close to the city and renting a car is pretty cheap. I went on a lot of hiking trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Canadians are very kind.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindsness and openness of the Canadians.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Be aware of the housing situation. You may not get on-campus housing, but there are a lot on facebook looking for roommates (+ airbnb). But it is expensive.
- The nature is amazing. Go on as many trips as possible!
- Try out different classes at the beginning, and be aware of the different expectations of exams and attendece that the profs have. I found it very nice to have a few courses where attendance were not a thing, as it gave me the possibility to travel more.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of school work (papers, mid-terms, class facilitations etc.).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to travel so much to the most beautiful places.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of school work, so I had to adjust a bit.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
